sections.title: Global Equities
sections.content: Global equities finished mixed-to-firmer as strong Nvidia earnings lifted technology while a hawkish Jackson Hole message capped gains. MSCI World rose roughly **+0.4%** (approx., verify before merging) and MSCI Developed Markets a similar **+0.4%** (approx., verify before merging), while MSCI Emerging Markets lagged near **-0.2%** (approx., verify before merging). The S&P 500 added **0.5%** to **7,711.76** and the MAG7 mega-cap cohort outperformed, up around **+1%** (approx., verify before merging) as the Nasdaq gained **0.9%** to **26,402.42**. Euro Stoxx 50 firmed about **+0.6%** to roughly **6,486** (approx., verify before merging), China's CSI 300 slipped to **4,609.18**, Hong Kong's Hang Seng was little changed near **25,585**, and Japan's Nikkei 225 rebounded to **66,405.56**.

sections.title: US Equities
sections.content:
US equities posted their first winning week in three, with the S&P 500 up **0.5%** to **7,711.76**, the Nasdaq Composite **0.9%** higher at **26,402.42** and the Dow Jones Industrial Average adding **0.5%** to **53,559.99**. The rally was led by mega-cap technology after Nvidia jumped nearly **9%** on Thursday, its results and AI-infrastructure outlook reviving enthusiasm for the semiconductor complex.

The week turned on Jackson Hole. In his debut symposium address, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warned that inflation remained too high, cautioning that better summer PCE and CPI prints did not signal a meaningful improvement in underlying trends, and left the door open to a rate hike.

The hawkish tone sparked a Friday pullback: the S&P 500 eased **0.25%**, the Nasdaq lost **0.52%** and small-caps fell more sharply as September rate-hike odds jumped to **57.5%** from **35.4%** a day earlier, leaving valuations and rate-sensitive leadership exposed.

sections.title: European Equities
sections.content:
European equities edged higher, outperforming a choppier Wall Street, with the pan-European STOXX Europe 600 up **0.46%** in local-currency terms and the Euro Stoxx 50 firmer at roughly **6,486** (approx., verify before merging).

Generally robust second-quarter corporate earnings underpinned sentiment, cushioning the region against a hawkish Jackson Hole and firmer global bond yields. Investors also weighed heightened Middle East tensions and higher oil prices as cross-currents into the close.

Sector dispersion reflected the macro backdrop, with energy names supported by firmer crude while higher discount-rate expectations weighed on growth and rate-sensitive plays. Steadier regional earnings momentum left European bourses comparatively resilient relative to the late-week US wobble.

sections.title: APAC Equities
sections.content:
Asian markets were mixed but steadier after the prior week's slump. Japan's Nikkei 225 rebounded to **66,405.56**, rising **0.41%** on Friday as information-technology, software, automakers and semiconductor-related shares tracked the Nvidia-led US tech rally, reversing part of the earlier chip-driven sell-off.

Chinese equities were subdued: the mainland CSI 300 slipped **0.46%** to **4,609.18**, leaving it broadly flat on the week, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng was little changed near **25,585**, up just **0.07%** on Friday.

The common thread was an AI-driven lift to North Asian tech set against a cautious pre-Jackson Hole tone, with the semiconductor cycle, the trajectory of US rates and Beijing's policy signals framing the near-term outlook.

sections.title: Foreign Exchange
sections.content:
The US dollar traded on the soft side for much of the week before finding support late on, as Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole message and the jump in September rate-hike odds lifted front-end yields and the greenback into the close.

The euro consolidated above **1.1500**, around six-week highs, helped by a softer dollar backdrop earlier in the week, while sterling was broadly flat, staying trapped in the **1.32–1.35** range that has defined much of 2026. The yen remained supported, with intervention concerns and a larger official footprint making investors think twice about JPY-funded carry trades.

The dominant driver was the shift in Fed rate-differential expectations, which reasserted the dollar's yield advantage after weeks of complacency and kept risk-sensitive and EM currencies more cautious into month-end.

sections.title: Commodities
sections.content:
Precious metals set the tone but paused for breath. Gold consolidated below **$4,600** after a run of strong gains, having advanced around **13%** over the month, underpinned by fiscal and debt-sustainability concerns and a renewed focus on currency debasement, before steadying ahead of Warsh's speech.

Energy firmed, with crude edging higher despite rising Gulf exports as Middle East tensions kept a geopolitical premium in play, reviving inflation worries just as the rate outlook turned more hawkish.

Agricultural markets stood out, with wheat and corn posting strong weekly gains, while base metals held broadly firm. The cross-asset read was that inflation-hedging demand and geopolitics continued to broaden the commodity bid even as real-yield expectations edged higher.

sections.title: Fixed Income
sections.content:
Sovereign yields rose as Jackson Hole reset the policy outlook. The 10-year UST yield climbed **4bp** to **4.72%** after Warsh's remarks, while the 30-year added **2bp** to **5.21%** and the 2-year sat near **4.34%**, with the front end most exposed to the hawkish repricing.

The key catalyst was Warsh's warning that inflation remained too high and his refusal to rule out a hike, which drove fed funds futures to price a **57.5%** chance of a September increase, up from **35.4%** the prior day, nudging the curve flatter.

Higher-for-longer rate expectations reinforced the strategic appeal of quality income, with investment-grade bonds offering more attractive yields. Credit tone stayed broadly firm, though richer valuations and elevated rate uncertainty argued for selectivity across IG and HY into month-end.
